table.purpose: Unresolved. The table's contents are heavily coded/obfuscated (e.g. col_012 appears to be text encoded with a letter-substitution cipher, and most columns carry opaque short codes). The row count (806), a near-unique numeric identifier, a future-dated date column, several small numeric measures and +/- flag columns do not match any identifiable real-world schema, so the table's meaning cannot be determined from the evidence alone. Its relationship to t02 and t03 is also unknown: no column shows accepted joins, so no foreign-key structure can be confirmed.

col_001.description: Near-unique integer (763 distinct in 806 rows, ~99% unique), no null-pattern structure and no joins to other tables. Plausibly a row identifier or an external reference number, but the values themselves carry no decodable meaning. Could also be a measured quantity (values 14,872–9,334,040) rather than an ID; the evidence does not distinguish these readings.

col_002.description: A date between 2045-04-18 and 2054-04-17, i.e. strictly future-dated relative to any plausible collection date, spread over ~9 years. Likely a due/maturity/expiry/scheduled date rather than an event record date, but nothing in the data confirms which.

col_005.description: Integer taking only the values 0, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096 (and possibly 4094) — powers of two (plus one apparent 4094 outlier). This strongly suggests a bitmask/flag field or a size class encoded as powers of 2, but the individual bit meanings cannot be determined.

col_009.description: Binary flag taking only '+' or '-' (82% null, '-' more common). A yes/present ('+') vs absent ('-') indicator, but what condition it indicates is unknown.

col_010.description: Binary flag taking only '+' or '-' (82% null), with the same null rate as col_009, suggesting the two flags are recorded together. What it indicates is unknown.

col_011.description: Binary flag taking only '+' or '-' (73% null). Same +/- convention as col_009/col_010; meaning unknown.

table.purpose: Per-observation or per-measurement records of astronomical objects (likely stars): each row references an object in t03 via col_001 and carries a date plus many mostly-null numeric measurement columns, several of which look like magnitudes (values ~4-13, some ~38) and censored text values like '<8.0'. The exact instrument/survey is unknown, and dates lie in 2037-2055, so the data may be synthetic or forecast-dated. Most columns cannot be pinned down beyond 'numeric measurement of the object'. The table is likely a child/detail table of t03 (objects) and possibly related to t01 via t03.

col_001.name: object_id
col_001.description: Identifier of the observed object; references t03.col_001 (many rows in t02 per object, ~302 distinct objects over 13908 rows).

col_002.name: observation_date
col_002.description: Date of the observation/measurement, ranging 2037-01-27 to 2055-03-04. Future dates suggest synthetic or forecast data; the column is clearly a date but what it dates is only tentatively the observation.

col_008.name: magnitude_band_2

col_034.name: censored_measurement_2
col_034.description: Text holding a number or censored value ('<38', '<78.5', '<41.5'); a measurement with upper limits, plausibly ~38-78 in some unit. Underlying quantity unresolved.

table.name: Patient
table.purpose: One row per record (likely a person or case) identified by an ID that is referenced by t02; the row carries a type/status code, a start date, and two future-dated milestone dates, plus a sign/indicator flag and a free-text category/notes field. The exact domain is unresolved, but the structure suggests a lifecycle/contract or membership record with planned future events. The future-dated columns (2047-2054) suggest either planned dates or a data-quality offset (e.g., dates shifted forward), which cannot be confirmed from the data alone.

col_001.name: record_id
col_001.description: Primary key of t03; unique integer identifier for each row. Referenced by t02.col_001 (many rows in t02 point to one row here), so this is the parent/master record ID.

col_002.name: record_type_code
col_002.description: Single-letter code classifying the record: 'D' (dominant, ~83%), 'J' (~16%), or empty (13 rows). Likely a type/category flag (e.g., D = individual/standard, J = joint/other). Exact meanings of D and J are unresolved.

col_003.name: start_date
col_003.description: Date associated with the record's origin, spanning 1968-2063 (future values suggest data-entry errors or shifted dates). Mostly distinct, roughly one per record — plausibly the record's start/birth/registration date.

col_004.name: planned_end_date
col_004.description: Future date (2047-2054), null in ~17% of rows, with heavy repetition of a few values (e.g., 2053-08-20 appears 64 times). Looks like a scheduled/contractual end or maturity date, possibly a default expiry assigned in batches. The uniformly future range could also indicate a systematic date offset.

col_005.name: event_date
col_005.description: Second future date (2028-2054), null in ~20% of rows, mostly distinct. A per-record future event date (e.g., review, renewal, or termination). Relationship to col_004 unclear; could alternatively be an actual vs. planned date.

col_006.name: sign_indicator
col_006.description: Short flag: '-' (~58%), '+' (~39%), empty, and '+(' (3 rows). Looks like a plus/minus indicator (e.g., credit/debit, active/inactive, or a sign of a quantity). Exact semantics unresolved.
